comment: This sentence, and the analysis of structural incentives preceding it, is the most valuable passage in the document, and it sits where a reader may treat it as background. If coordination is a political economy problem, then a reference architecture - a technical instrument - cannot on its own resolve it, and the guidance should say so plainly rather than leaving the inference to the reader.

public.text: This sentence, and the analysis of structural incentives preceding it, is the most valuable passage in the document, and it sits where a reader may treat it as background. If coordination is a political economy problem, then a reference architecture - a technical instrument - cannot on its own resolve it, and the guidance should say so plainly rather than leaving the inference to the reader.
public.suggestedRevision: Move this analysis into the introduction as a framing statement and draw the consequence explicitly: because the obstacle is an incentive structure, shared infrastructure will not emerge from voluntary alignment and requires instruments that change the incentives - obligation, enforcement, separation of roles, recurrent financing and dispute resolution. This supplies the rationale that the governance and financing chapters currently lack.
